Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=\sqrt{9x+1}$ that is closest to the point $(8,0).$ Do not round the answer.

$x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(8,0)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
S=(x-8)^{2}+{y}^{2}.
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=\sqrt{9x+1}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & =(x-8)^{2}+{y}^{2} \\  & =(x-8)^{2}+(\sqrt{9x+1})^{2} \\  & =(x-8)^{2}+9x+1 \\  & ={x}^{2}-16x+64+9x+1 \\  & ={x}^{2}-7x+65.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x-7 & =0 \\ 2x & =7 \\ x & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(x)=2>0.$ Therefore, $x=\frac{7}{2}$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $x=\frac{7}{2}.$
